_comment: Clients of the conversation between Chris and the box (H-016, docs/conversation.md). Each client has its own permissions: read (read entries), write (append a message), ask (append a question for Claude/search), start_task, answer (reply to a question from Claude), approve, run_job, research (ask a research question: one Claude run, counted against JOB_CLAUDE_CAP). The `kitt` client (H-018, docs/kitt.md) has no token: it is the app on loopback, recognised by its service account and by Chris's identity from the gate; its screens map to permissions as chat = read+write+ask, jobs = read+run_job (run, pause, resume), approvals = approve, usage and logs = read. Removing one switches that screen's actions off in the app. Its on/off switch is on the homelab page. An action without the permission is refused and logged. Read again on every request: no restart needed. A client authenticates to the loopback door with the token in /etc/homelab/chat-<name>-token. `tasks_per_day` caps the tasks (and builds) a client may start per day; above it nothing starts (default: CLIENT_TASKS_PER_DAY in inbox.conf). Nothing here can grant SSH keys, memory edits or merges on homelab: those exist for no client.
